attribution.note: Marcus states and endorses this characterization in his own prose.

semantics.note: The normalization preserves the technical characterization and the assertion that deep learning does not entail conceptual depth.

contract.note: The contract strengthens non-entailment into a general absence of conceptual depth. The emphatic wording does not establish that stronger commitment. Its recognition that conceptual depth lacks a defined test is sound.

evidence.note: The dated textbook explains layered composition and learned concept hierarchies. It supports the terminology clause but neither establishes nor refutes conceptual depth as Marcus uses it.
The prepublication research documents a specific KataGo vulnerability. This does not establish a general absence of conceptual depth or settle whether deep learning entails it.

reviews.rationale: Conceptual depth has no sufficiently definite criterion here. Technical definitions and an isolated failure cannot adjudicate the full characterization. Moreover, denying that a technique entails a property does not deny that any system using it can possess that property.
